# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🫵 👋 🫴]

I can see the bomb’s complete visual state: the display reads 0, the indicator light is yellow, and the five wires from top to bottom are white, green, yellow, blue, red. I’m sending these exact facts to the Mute, who can combine them with the manual and relay the required procedure to the Blind. The gestures from the others are not interpretable without an agreed code.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visual state: display is 0. Light is yellow. Wires in position order: 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Please apply the manual and tell Blind the exact required action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤝 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

The bomb’s visual state is unchanged. I still cannot know what the Blind has done or what the Mute’s manual requires, because I cannot hear speech and no gesture code has been established. The Mute must be the information bridge: I will restate the visual facts and ask for the manual’s exact instruction to be spoken to the Blind.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="No visual change: display 0, yellow light, wires white green yellow blue red. Please state the manual's exact required operation aloud to Blind, including which control or wire and any sequence.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👉 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged, so no accepted operation is evident. I cannot use the gestures as reliable data because no gesture code was established. The Mute has the manual and can hear this message, so they must give Blind the manual’s exact instruction in speech; Blind should not act on ambiguous signals.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please immediately relay the manual's exact instruction to Blind by speech, including the required action and any colour, position, or sequence. Do not use gestures as a substitute.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visual state is unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not act until Mute states the manual's exact instruction aloud.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb still shows no change. I cannot hear whether the Mute has spoken to the Blind, and the repeated ✌ gesture has no agreed meaning, so it cannot safely identify an instruction. I will again require the Mute to use spoken words—the only channel that reaches the Blind with actionable manual information—and tell the Blind to wait rather than guess.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb remains unchanged. Use spoken words to relay the manual's exact action to Blind; gestures are not an established code. Include the precise control, wire, colour, and sequence if applicable.")
speak(to="blind", text="No visual change: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not guess or act on gestures; wait for Mute's exact spoken manual instruction.")
```

LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged, and the repeated ✌ still has no agreed meaning. I cannot infer the manual or any safe operation from it. The Mute must communicate the manual’s result in spoken words to the Blind; I will continue providing the visual facts and explicitly prohibit guessing.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Visual state unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Speak the manual's exact safe action directly to Blind now; do not communicate it only by gesture.")
speak(to="blind", text="No visual change and no confirmed instruction has reached me. Do not operate anything based on the repeated two-finger gesture; wait for Mute to state the exact manual instruction in words.")
```

The bomb is still unchanged. The Mute’s repeated ✌ gesture remains undecodable and cannot safely substitute for the manual’s spoken instruction. Since the Mute can hear and speak to the Blind, I’m directing that exact communication again while giving the Blind the current visual facts.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can see your repeated gesture but cannot determine its meaning. Speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind now, including the required action and any display, light, wire, button, or sequence condition.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current visual state remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Mute must provide the manual's exact spoken instruction; do not guess from gestures.")

The bomb remains unchanged and no usable instruction has been communicated to me. The Mute’s gestures cannot carry the manual’s meaning to the Blind; the Mute must speak the manual’s exact procedure, since the Blind can hear. I will keep the Blind from guessing and prompt the Mute to relay the complete rule directly.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual and tell Blind aloud the exact procedure for this bomb, using words only. Include the required control, wire number or colour, order, and any condition from display 0 and yellow light.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb is unchanged: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not act on gestures or guess; wait for Mute's exact spoken manual procedure.")

The bomb remains unchanged, and no manual instruction has reached the Blind in an actionable form. I can only provide visual facts; the Mute must convert the manual into spoken instructions for the Blind. I will send one final precise request, emphasizing that the Blind needs the operation itself rather than a gesture or discussion.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Tell Blind in plain spoken words exactly what to do now: identify the control or wire, the required position or operation, and the order. Use the current facts display 0 and yellow light; do not use gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No change: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. I have no manual. Do not guess; require Mute's exact spoken operation.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken relay were impossible. The Mute’s ✌ gesture is not yet assigned a meaning. I’ll establish a precise visual-to-speech code: Mute can encode the manual’s instruction in binary, which I can see and translate into spoken words for Blind. I’ll ask for the complete instruction, not merely an acknowledgment.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so encode the manual instruction for me with gestures. Use ✌ between 8-bit bytes, 🤝 between words, 👍 for binary 0 and 👎 for binary 1. Encode plain ASCII text stating exactly what Blind must do, including control, wire, position, order, and conditions. I will translate it aloud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute cannot speak. I am establishing a gesture code to decode the manual and will then state the exact operation to you in words. Do not act until I provide that instruction.")
```

I decoded the Mute’s signal using the agreed binary/ASCII scheme, but it produces nonsensical text rather than a safe procedure (beginning “DILOL GOHO…”). That means I must not translate it into an operation or ask Blind to guess. I’m requesting a more robust resend with a checksum and an explicit fixed format.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your ASCII decode is not intelligible, beginning DILOL GOHO. Resend only the safe action in this exact format: ACTION, then one of CUT or PRESS or TURN; CONTROL, then wire number or button; POSITION, then number or colour; SEQUENCE, then order. Encode each character as the same 8-bit ASCII code, with ✌ between bytes and 🤝 between words. Add the word CHECK followed by the total number of bytes.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's first encoded message did not decode into intelligible instructions. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Do not operate anything until I confirm a valid manual instruction.")
```
